_status: PROPOSED — NOT calibrated, NOT signed off.
_note: Per CLAUDE.md thresholds and tunables live in config, never hardcoded. These are data-layer and dry-run tunables: which underlying we screen, the DTE band we ask the contracts endpoint for, the snapshot feed, and page sizes. None of them is a trading judgement — the DTE band was chosen so a SPY monthly expiry falls inside it, not because 21-45 days is the right place to sell premium. The CALLER loads this file and passes the mapping in (same discipline as GB_INTERFACES.md 6a); no module holds a copy.
_dte_note: The band the LIVE pipeline asks the contracts endpoint for. dte_min_days is 0 because same-day expiries are in scope; dte_max_days is a wide outer bound, because the binding constraint is NOT this number — it is `max_expiry_date` in config/thresholds.governor.SCORED.json, and the caller clamps this window to it. One owner for the scored bound, and this band cannot silently disagree with it.
_fixture_note: Recording-only. scripts/record_fixtures.py narrows to a strike band and one option type so that the recorded pagination sample is a COMPLETE run — page 2 terminates — while still spanning every expiry in its window, which is what makes the nearest-expiry-first ordering visible across the page boundary. It keeps its OWN DTE band so that re-recording reproduces the committed fixtures byte for byte rather than following the live band around. These never reach a live run.
